patient_summary:
Hello there, it looks like you're feeling weak and shaky, and you're having trouble breathing when you walk around. This has been going on for a while, but it's gotten worse recently. You've had some other health problems in the past, like heart disease, high blood pressure, and diabetes. You also had a problem with your heart a few years ago, and you've had some infections in your urinary system.

We're not sure exactly what's causing your shortness of breath, but we think it might be related to your heart. We'll ask your mom to help us review your medical history so we can understand more. We might also do a stress test to see how your heart is working.

We know you have high blood pressure, but we're not sure if you're taking any medicine for it. We need you to tell us the names of any medicines you're taking, so we can make sure you're getting the right treatment.

We also know you have diabetes, but we're not sure if you're taking any medicine for it. We'll need to ask you more about your diabetes to help us decide what to do next.

Right now, we're going to check your blood pressure and do some tests to see what's going on. If you feel weak or shaky, or if you have any other symptoms, please let us know right away. We're here to help you feel better.
caregiver_checklist: Check patient’s blood pressure and pulse at home and report to the care team.
Watch for signs of shortness of breath, chest pain, or palpitations.
Call the care team if the patient experiences chest pain or shortness of breath.
Schedule a stress test to evaluate for possible coronary artery disease.
Check the patient’s blood sugar levels and report to the care team.
Watch for signs of diabetes complications such as infections or nerve damage.
Call the care team if the patient experiences any new symptoms.
Schedule a follow-up appointment in 2 weeks to review progress and adjust treatment as needed.
Check for signs of hyperlipidemia such as skin changes or abdominal pain.
Watch for signs of urinary tract infections such as fever or cloudy urine.
Call the care team if the patient experiences any new symptoms or signs of infections.
child_explanation: You have a tummy ache and feel weak and shaky, you know? It's like your body is tired and needs some help. Grown-ups and doctors are taking care of you. They want to find out what's making you feel this way. You might be a bit confused, but you're safe. The doctors will check you and ask lots of questions to understand better. They'll also look at your past history to help figure things out. It might take a few days to find the answer, but you're in good hands.
source_text: CHIEF COMPLAINT:,  Weak and shaky.,HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:,  The patient is a 75-year-old, Caucasian female who comes in today with complaint of feeling weak and shaky.  When questioned further, she described shortness of breath primarily with ambulation.  She denies chest pain.  She denies cough, hemoptysis, dyspnea, and wheeze.  She denies syncope, presyncope, or palpitations.  Her symptoms are fairly longstanding but have been worsening as of late.,PAST MEDICAL HISTORY:,  She has had a fairly extensive past medical history but is a somewhat poor historian and is unable to provide details about her history.  She states that she has underlying history of heart disease but is not able to elaborate to any significant extent.  She also has a history of hypertension and type II diabetes but is not currently taking any medication.  She has also had a history of pulmonary embolism approximately four years ago, hyperlipidemia, peptic ulcer disease, and recurrent urinary tract infections.  Surgeries include an appendectomy, cesarean section, cataracts, and hernia repair.,CURRENT MEDICATIONS:,  She is on two different medications, neither of which she can remember the name and why she is taking it.,ALLERGIES: , She has no known medical allergies.,FAMILY HISTORY:,  Remarkable for coronary artery disease, stroke, and congestive heart failure.,SOCIAL HISTORY:,  She is a widow, lives alone.  Denies any tobacco or alcohol use.,REVIEW OF SYSTEMS:,  Dyspnea on exertion.
